Order 
This is first application filed under Section 482 of B.N.S.S., 2023/Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail on behalf of applicant Prem Chand Singh who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.24/2025 dated 21/02/2025 registered at Police Station Economic Offence Wing, district Bhopal, for the offence punishable under Sections 406, 420 and 120-B of IPC.

This first anticipatory bail application has been argued on the grounds that applicant is being falsely implicated in a series of cases without there being any evidence about his involvement and to show the malafide intention of prosecuting agency EOW/ED, the bail orders passed in different crime numbers registered against the applicant have been filed as Annexures A12 to A17; it is also submitted that no authority was given by the applicant in favour of Shri M. K. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17273 2 MCRC-12893-2025 Singh to execute a lease-deed in the year 2007 regarding a property situated at Pachmarhi; Shri M. K. Singh, the then property manager of Jabalpur Diocese, was acting on his own volition to execute the questioned lease-deed; the applicant did not authorize the renewal of said lease-deed either; the said property was not under the sole Prem Chand Singh (P.C. Singh) vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72778212/
1 jurisdiction of Jabalpur Diocese as reflected from Annexure A3 and it gave simultaneous jurisdiction to Bhopal (Indore) Diocese; it is being claimed by the prosecution that no resolution regarding execution of lease-deed of the property of Pachmarhi was passed on 30.1.2009 and this fact itself explains that the rent agreement was executed by Shri M. K. Singh fraudulently and without having any consultation with the applicant; the signatures of applicant are also not there on this rent-deed as can be seen from Annexures A4 and A5; it is further submitted that the applicant became the Bishop of Jabalpur Diocese in the year 2004 and prior to that period the earlier Bishop Shri Sunil Cak had initiated the proceedings to give this property on rent for which letter dated 14.7.2000 (Annexure A7) was written and on 8.2.2001, Rs.6,60,000/- were received by Shri Sunil Cak from Shri Shailendra Roy as lease rent for a period of ten years for this property under Annexures A8 and A9; an agreement in this regard was though executed on 1.4.2001 and it was later rescinded,
nevertheless, Shri M. K. Singh continued to take care of Pachmarhi property; it is, therefore, claimed that even if Shri M. K. Singh was illegally renting out the property, no criminality can be assigned to the present applicant and no useful purpose will be served to send him into custody when he is a reputed citizen and is willing to cooperate with the investigation.

sentences.text: A request has, therefore, been made to allow the application.

State through EOW has opposed the application claiming that the Power of Attorney executed in favour of applicant on 19.02.2007 specifically defined the rights of applicant allowing him to grant lease of property only under prior NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17273 3 MCRC-12893-2025 approval of NDTA (Nagpur Diocise Trust Association); applicant was appointed Shri M.K. Singh as Secretary, Diocesan Property Committees, and then issued an authority letter on 17.12.2012 in favour of Shri M.K. Singh authorizing him to sign the lease renewal papers; it is to be investigated in whose favour the advanced rent was deposited; it has, therefore, been argued that the present case is not of the nature where the relief of anticipatory should be given; the complainant in this case was a member of NDTA for a period of 2006 to 2008 and the property belonging to that institution was fraudulently and without any authority given on lease.
A request has, therefore, been made to dismiss the anticipatory bail.

From the documents available in the case diary and also the document which have been relied upon as annexures by the applicant, it appears prima facie, that applicant was not executing any lease deed of the property in question, nor was he giving any authority to Shri M.K. Singh to execute the lease deed.

Merely by the act of appointing Shri M.K. Singh as Secretary, Property Committee, it is difficult to arrive to the conclusion that applicant was in connivance with him to dishonestly rent out the property.
Having considered the role of applicant reflected from the documents in execution of questioned lease deed, this Court is of opinion that applicant deserves to be released on anticipatory bail.

So far the apprehension of respondent regarding prospective non-cooperation of applicant during investigation is concerned, the respondent is always at liberty to raise this issue and request for appropriate relief.
Heard the submissions and perused the case diary.

It is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant shall be enlarged on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer for his appearance before him during the course of investigation or before the trial Court concerned during trial, as the case may be.
It is further directed that the applicant shall abide by all the conditions as enumerated under Section 482(2) of the BNSS.
In case applicant fails to co- operate in investigation, this bail order may be considered for cancellation.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands disposed of .
